application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A type-safe, lightweight HTTP fetch client with automatic JSON body handling, response parsing, retries, timeouts, hooks, and normalized errors.
application.purpose: Provide a friendly, typed fetch wrapper used across browser and Node environments that handles request serialization, query/baseURL merging, response type detection, retry/timeout, error normalization, and lifecycle hooks.

domains.name: HTTP client core
domains.description: Core request execution: building fetch options, baseURL/query handling, headers merging, and response parsing.

domains.name: Retries, timeouts and aborts
domains.description: Retry behavior on retryable status codes, optional retry delay, timeouts via AbortController, and abort handling.

domains.name: Error normalization
domains.description: Construction of normalized FetchError values carrying request, options, response, data and status details.

domains.name: Lifecycle hooks
domains.description: onRequest/onRequestError/onResponse/onResponseError hooks (single or arrays) invoked around the fetch lifecycle.

domains.name: Body serialization and response typing
domains.description: Detecting JSON-serializable payloads, auto-stringifying bodies, and inferring responseType from content-type.

terminology.meaning: The main fetch client function returned by createFetch; also exported as `fetch` alias; callable with a typed generic and responseType.
Variant of $fetch that resolves the full FetchResponse (including _data, status, headers) instead of just the parsed data.
Augmented Response carrying a `_data` field with the parsed body.
Internal context object flowing through the pipeline: request, options, response (optional), error (optional).
Expected parse mode of the response: json, text, blob, arrayBuffer, stream (defaults detected from Content-Type).
Normalized error class extending Error with request, options, response, data, status/statusText/statusCode/statusMessage accessors.
Base URL prepended to relative request paths (combined with query/params).
Query string parameters merged from defaults and input; params is the deprecated alias.
HTTP method carrying a body (PATCH/POST/PUT/DELETE) used to decide body serialization and default retry behavior.
onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse and onResponseError callbacks (single or array) used for lifecycle interception.
Retry on retryable HTTP status codes with optional numeric or context-based delay; default statuses 408/409/425/429/500/502/503/504.
Millisecond limit on the request aborts the operation with a TimeoutError.

entityAnnotations.businessMeaning: Usage example demonstrating typed response inference via ofetch generics (e.g. typed Repo).
Ad-hoc experiment script calling $fetch against a 500 endpoint to observe error handling.
Builds a normalized FetchError (message plus request/options/response/data/status accessors) for a failed request.
Identifies HTTP methods expected to carry a request body (PATCH/POST/PUT/DELETE).
Determines whether a request body value can be safely JSON-serialized; non-serializable values (FormData, URLSearchParams, streams, etc.) bypass JSON handling.
Infers the response parse type (json/text/blob/stream) from the response Content-Type header.
Merges default and per-call options, headers, and query/params into a resolved options object.
Combines HeadersInit from defaults and input into a single Headers instance (input overrides defaults).
Executes a lifecycle hook (or array of hooks) against the current FetchContext.
Main factory that builds a configured $fetch client with default options, implementing the full request pipeline, retries, hooks, response parsing and error throwing.
Handles failed requests: applies retry rules (unless aborted), then creates and throws the normalized FetchError.
Creates a Node-compatible fetch (node-fetch-native based), optionally with a keep-alive HTTP/HTTPS agent via FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE.
Test helper that aborts an in-flight $fetch call while retry is enabled to verify abort behavior.

applicationFacts: Two entry points: universal src/index.ts (uses globalThis.fetch) and Node-specific src/node.ts (falls back to node-fetch-native).
Auto-stringifies JSON-serializable bodies for payload methods, setting application/json content-type and accept by default; FormData/URLSearchParams and streams bypass JSON handling.
Merges baseURL/query into relative request strings and serializes query parameters after defaults and input are merged.
Retries failed requests on configurable retryable status codes (default set) with optional numeric retry count/delay, except when aborted; payload-method requests default to zero retries.
Applies an AbortController-based timeout that aborts the request with a TimeoutError.
Parses responses by detected or explicit responseType; json parsing uses destr by default or a user-supplied parseResponse.
Throws normalized FetchError for 4xx/5xx responses unless ignoreResponseError is set; exposes request/options/response/data and status accessors.
Supports lifecycle hooks (onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError) as single callbacks or arrays, run sequentially per stage.
$fetch.raw returns the full FetchResponse (with _data); $fetch itself returns only the parsed data; $fetch.native exposes the underlying fetch.
$fetch.create builds a new client with merged global and default options; used for deep-merged defaults tests.
Null-body responses (101/204/205/304) and HEAD requests skip body parsing.
Built with unbuild (CJS) with entries src/index and src/node; undici is external; tests use Vitest with an in-process H3 server.
